summary: A full packet before the first trade (no last traded price) with a book, then the first traded packet: no Quote frame shows a zero price, while the Depth holder gets the book with ltp 0; the traded packet reaches both.

notes: Lead decision (bk-b phase B, round 2 item c): a full packet whose lastTradedPrice is 0 (proto3: not sent) marks the price absent, so no LTP or Quote frame goes out for it; its book still reaches Depth holders with ltp 0 (the 1.0.6 depth-before-first-quote rule).

The web publishes the Quote topic for the no-trade packet with ltp 0 and a change of -1495.0 (ltp - close with ltp 0); the Quote client's silence names that frame (missing-frame, web defect, approved). The Depth frame leaves out the trade time and the open, high, low, volume, last quantity and average price the packet never sent (feed/bridge/snapshot.rs sent_without_price); the web's packet-time ltt and zeros are declared web defects.

Before the first trade the packet carries no last traded price (proto3 0); the web publishes ltp 0 and a change of ltp - close from it (-1495.0, -100.0%), a price and a change no trade made. Before the first trade the packet has no lastTradeTime and the web sends its packet time as ltt, a time no trade happened at; the desktop leaves ltt out.
On the traded packets the web sends the broker's trade time in epoch seconds as ltt, where feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md); the desktop sends ms.

Before the first trade the web publishes a Quote frame with ltp 0 and a change from it; the desktop sends a Quote holder no frame with a zero price (the book goes to the Depth holder). Lead decision (bk-b phase B round 2, item c): where the web publishes ltp 0, web defect.

A cash equity's packet carries no OI (proto3 writes oi 0); the web sends that 0 as oi and open_interest instead of leaving them out (web openalgo#2376). The desktop counts OI on the derivative segments only. Lead decision: web zeros for values the stream did not send are left out, web defect.
